bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to transportation; modifying certain requirements for trunk highway project development, scoping, and alternatives analysis; establishing a working group; requiring a report; appropriating money; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 161.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[161.1615] PROJECT SCOPING AND DEVELOPMENT.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Major highway project" has the meaning given in section 174.56, subdivision 1, paragraph (b).

(c) "Principal transportation system users" means each of the following users of surface transportation right-of-way for transportation purposes: motorists, commercial vehicles, pedestrians, bicyclists and other nonmotorized vehicle operators, and transit users and vehicles.

Subd. 2.

Application.

(a) The requirements in this section apply to a major highway project on the trunk highway system that:

(1) involves construction, reconstruction, bridge replacement, or acquisition of permanent right-of-way;

(2) adds highway traffic capacity or provides for grade separation of motor vehicle traffic at an intersection, excluding auxiliary lanes with a length of less than 2,500 feet; or

(3) requires an environmental impact statement under chapter 116D for the project.

(b) Except for a project under paragraph (a), clause (1), the requirements in this section do not apply to reconditioning, resurfacing, rehabilitation, preventive maintenance, other routine infrastructure maintenance activities or projects, and associated capital set-asides.

(c) The requirements in this section are effective for a project that first enters the appropriate state or metropolitan transportation improvement program for fiscal year 2031 or a subsequent year. This section does not apply to a project that (1) was included in the appropriate transportation improvement program, or (2) has submitted for approval a geometric layout before July 1, 2030.

Subd. 3.

Purpose and need statement.

(a) The purpose and need statement established by the commissioner for a project under this section must:

(1) allow for consideration of alternatives as provided in subdivision 4; and

(2) provide for evaluation of impacts of safety, accessibility, and mobility for principal transportation system users.

(b) The purpose and need statement must not identify, tacitly presume, or preclude a specific improvement to address the stated transportation deficiency or problem.

Subd. 4.

Project alternatives.

(a) The project development process for a project under this section must include identification and analysis of a suitably comprehensive set of design alternatives to address the project purpose and need. The process must:

(1) incorporate alternatives that improve access to destinations for principal transportation system users;

(2) include evaluation of appropriate multimodal alternatives;

(3) include evaluation of at least one alternative that reduces traffic lanes, reduces the area of the road right-of-way, or lowers the functional classification of the road;

(4) consider relevant traffic models, safety analyses, air quality analyses, and other data;

(5) consider coordination of transportation investments in the corridor, including transit and active transportation projects, to maximize project delivery efficiency and minimize negative impacts to system users, local units of government, and affected property owners; and

(6) conform with state transportation system goals under section 174.01, subdivision 2.

(b) The project development process must not conflict with the requirements under chapter 116D and the National Environmental Policy Act under United States Code, title 42, section 4331, et seq.

Sec. 2. PROJECT SCOPING AND DEVELOPMENT WORKING GROUP.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of transportation.

(c) "Working group" means the Project Scoping and Development Working Group established in this section.

Subd. 2.

Establishment.

The commissioner must convene a working group to develop a comprehensive framework to implement the trunk highway project scoping and development requirements under Minnesota Statutes, section 161.1615. The commissioner must seek to collaborate with the Center for Transportation Studies at the University of Minnesota to lead the working group.

Subd. 3.

Membership.

The commissioner of transportation must solicit the following to participate as members in the working group:

(1) Department of Transportation district staff who perform planning and engineering functions;

(2) metropolitan planning organizations;

(3) county engineers;

(4) city engineers; and

(5) individuals with relevant experience and expertise in transportation planning, multimodal highway project development, and cost-benefit analysis, which may include but is not limited to the following areas:

(i) multimodal transportation planning;

(ii) transit operations and planning;

(iii) pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure design and planning;

(iv) land use planning;

(v) highway traffic modeling;

(vi) highway safety analysis; and

(vii) highway right-sizing or roadway reconfiguration.

Subd. 4.

Duties.

At a minimum, the working group must:

(1) evaluate and make recommendations on project scoping and development practices by the Department of Transportation; and

(2) develop and propose an updated methodology for cost-benefit analyses performed to comprehensively evaluate major trunk highway project investments.

Subd. 5.

Administration.

Upon request of the working group, the commissioner must provide administrative and technical support.

Subd. 6.

Report.

By February 1, 2027, the working group must submit a report on trunk highway project scoping and development to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over transportation policy and finance. At a minimum, the report must summarize the results of the working group and provide information on each of the activities specified in subdivision 4.

Subd. 7.

Expiration.

The working group expires June 30, 2027.

Sec. 3. APPROPRIATION; PROJECT DEVELOPMENT.

$....... in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the trunk highway fund to the commissioner of transportation for the Project Scoping and Development Working Group under section 2 and to implement the project scoping and development requirements under Minnesota Statutes, section 161.1615.

(1) allow for consideration of alternatives as provided in subdivision 4; and
(2) provide for evaluation of impacts of safety, accessibility, and mobility for principal transportation system users.
(b) The purpose and need statement must not identify, tacitly presume, or preclude a specific improvement to address the stated transportation deficiency or problem.
Subd. 4.
Project alternatives.

(a) The project development process for a project under this section must include identification and analysis of a suitably comprehensive set of design alternatives to address the project purpose and need. The process must:
(1) incorporate alternatives that improve access to destinations for principal transportation system users;
(2) include evaluation of appropriate multimodal alternatives;
(3) include evaluation of at least one alternative that reduces traffic lanes, reduces the area of the road right-of-way, or lowers the functional classification of the road;
(4) consider relevant traffic models, safety analyses, air quality analyses, and other data;

(5) consider coordination of transportation investments in the corridor, including transit and active transportation projects, to maximize project delivery efficiency and minimize negative impacts to system users, local units of government, and affected property owners; and
(6) conform with state transportation system goals under section 174.01, subdivision 2.
(b) The project development process must not conflict with the requirements under chapter 116D and the National Environmental Policy Act under United States Code, title 42, section 4331, et seq.
PROJECT SCOPING AND DEVELOPMENT WORKING GROUP.
Subdivision 1.
Definitions.
(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.
(b) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of transportation.
(c) "Working group" means the Project Scoping and Development Working Group established in this section.
Subd. 2.
Establishment.

The commissioner must convene a working group to develop a comprehensive framework to implement the trunk highway project scoping and development requirements under Minnesota Statutes, section 161.1615. The commissioner must seek to collaborate with the Center for Transportation Studies at the University of Minnesota to lead the working group.
Subd. 3.
Membership.
The commissioner of transportation must solicit the following to participate as members in the working group:
(1) Department of Transportation district staff who perform planning and engineering functions;
(2) metropolitan planning organizations;
(3) county engineers;
(4) city engineers; and

(5) individuals with relevant experience and expertise in transportation planning, multimodal highway project development, and cost-benefit analysis, which may include but is not limited to the following areas:
(i) multimodal transportation planning;
(ii) transit operations and planning;
(iii) pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure design and planning;
(iv) land use planning;
(v) highway traffic modeling;
(vi) highway safety analysis; and
(vii) highway right-sizing or roadway reconfiguration.
Subd. 4.
Duties.
At a minimum, the working group must:
(1) evaluate and make recommendations on project scoping and development practices by the Department of Transportation; and
(2) develop and propose an updated methodology for cost-benefit analyses performed to comprehensively evaluate major trunk highway project investments.
Subd. 5.
Administration.
Upon request of the working group, the commissioner must provide administrative and technical support.
Subd. 6.
Report.

By February 1, 2027, the working group must submit a report on trunk highway project scoping and development to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over transportation policy and finance. At a minimum, the report must summarize the results of the working group and provide information on each of the activities specified in subdivision 4.
Subd. 7.
Expiration.
The working group expires June 30, 2027.
APPROPRIATION; PROJECT DEVELOPMENT.

$....... in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the trunk highway fund to the commissioner of transportation for the Project Scoping and Development Working Group under section 2 and to implement the project scoping and development requirements under Minnesota Statutes, section 161.1615.
